claims.claim: Ireland introduced a 15-euro-cent levy on plastic bags in 2002, and consumption fell roughly 90 percent shortly afterward.
claims.episode_span: Ireland introduced the first nationwide levy in 2002 at fifteen cents per bag; consumption fell roughly 90 percent within months.

claims.supporting_quote: In Ireland, the introduction of a €0.15 levy on plastic bags in 2002 led to a 90% reduction in usage within weeks

claims.claim: The 2011 UK Environment Agency life-cycle assessment found a cotton bag must be reused 131 times to match a single-use plastic bag's climate impact.
claims.episode_span: a widely cited 2011 UK Environment Agency study, calculated that a cotton tote bag must be reused at least 131 times to produce lower environmental impacts than the single-use polyethylene bag it replaced
claims.source_title: Paper, Plastic or Reusable? | STANFORD magazine
claims.supporting_quote: An exhaustive Environment Agency (U.K.) report from 2011 found that paper bags must be reused at least three times to negate their higher climate-warming potential (compared with that of plastic bags). A cotton bag would have to be reused 131 times to break even with a plastic bag, in terms of the climate impact of producing each bag.

claims.claim: Analysts studying bag bans found households switched to purchasing other plastic bags: garbage-bag sales rose sharply after plastic grocery bags were banned.
claims.episode_span: A few analysts noted that households might simply switch to other plastic products, but those cautions remained secondary to the visible reduction in discarded bags.
claims.source_title: Are Plastic Bag Bans Garbage? : Planet Money : NPR
claims.supporting_quote: "What I found was that sales of garbage bags actually skyrocketed after plastic grocery bags were banned," she says. This was particularly the case for small, 4-gallon bags, which saw a 120 percent increase in sales after bans went into effect.

claims.claim: After bag bans, households bought purpose-made trash liners, offsetting about 30 percent of the plastic the bans eliminated.
claims.episode_span: Once the thin grocery bag disappeared, many households began purchasing purpose-made trash-bin liners.
claims.source_title: Are Plastic Bag Bans Garbage? : Planet Money : NPR
claims.supporting_quote: "So about 30 percent of the plastic that was eliminated by the ban comes back in the form of thicker garbage bags," Taylor says.

claims.claim: Cotton bags are typically used far fewer times than the reuse threshold: an Environment Agency-commissioned study found the average cotton bag is used only 51 times.
claims.episode_span: Most cotton totes were used far fewer times before being lost or discarded.
claims.supporting_quote: A study commissioned by the United Kingdom Environment Agency in 2005 found that the average cotton bag is used only 51 times before being thrown away.
